CHIEF COMPLAINT
Acne on the face.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Kayla Ward is a 19-year-old here for evaluation of acne located on the face that started approximately two years ago and is present most every day. She reports the acne is not too bad on the chest or back. She has been using Persa-gel and washing regularly with some helpful effect. She denies associated symptoms including itching, bleeding, or pain. Her current skin care routine consists of: morning - wiping her face with water and a washcloth, occasionally using an elf super clarity cleanser if she feels greasy; evening - using elf super clarity cleanser, followed by a toner and Persa-gel. She reports today is a good day for her acne. She denies acne flaring with her periods. Mother reports the biggest flare occurred when patient started school sports in the fall due to sweating. Mother also notes that despite patient doing a good job with the facial care regimen, it has not helped as much as desired.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies itching, bleeding, or pain associated with acne. Gets regular period for approximately two years. Acne does not flare with menses.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No additional past medical history.

MEDICATIONS
Persa-gel, elf super clarity cleanser, toner, elf facial cleanser as needed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
No additional family history.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives with parents and sister. Pets include a dog, bird, and bunnies. Currently in 7th grade. Plays basketball, volleyball, and tap. Wears sunscreen in summer, SPF 30.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Full exam performed except under underwear and bra. Multiple benign nevi on trunk and extremities. Scattered skin-colored papules, open and closed comedones, and erythematous papules on face primarily on forehead with some on central cheeks and chin. Chest and back relatively spared. Remainder of examination normal.

RESULTS
Mild to moderate acne, mostly comedonal with small inflammatory component. Multiple benign moles noted on arms, legs, back, and abdomen with no worrisome features.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Started topical acne therapy. Morning regimen: wash face with mild cleanser, apply noncomedogenic moisturizer with sunscreen SPF 30 or higher. Evening regimen: wash face with mild cleanser, allow to dry, apply adapalene 0.1% cream in thin layer to areas of acne, starting a few nights per week and slowly increasing to nightly use (can substitute with over-the-counter gel if cost or insurance prohibitive), followed by Clean and Clear Persa-gel and noncomedogenic moisturizer. Counseled that adapalene may cause sensitivity and dryness or irritation; sunscreen needed when outside. Benign moles will be monitored. Follow-up appointment in 6 months to assess progress. Patient instructed to call office with any questions or concerns before next visit.
